Small and readable, but: design_with mutates the sibling module's global rd.SUBS by magic index 4 (alu.py:33-38) with no check that it is 'wood-smooth-rods', so a reorder in selfrep-redesign silently replaces the wrong substitution (mutation M5 showed this goes unnoticed); sys.path manipulation at import across three sibling trees (alu.py:13-15); test file imports selfrep_rodbeam only via alu's side effect; run.py is an unstructured script recomputing min_diameter three times. 2.
evidence.claims: Checked each README Results number against results.txt and my recomputation: 0.192 mm, 10.4 mm, 16.9 mm, 10.3-10.5 mm over 68-72 GPa, 12.3 mm at 0.1 mm, 0.2 mm feasibility, 39.5/37.8/28.7%, 4538->3608 g, 2360/2190/1828 g: all backed. Assumptions (moduli, load, 12 mm limit, router-cut bar surface) are stated as assumptions, 'computed only; no rod was built' and AI assistance are stated. One misleading comparison: 'the aluminium design imports ... 530 g more than the steel-rod design' counts only makeable-line stock; the steel rods (930 g) are imported too, as vitamins, so total imported mass actually falls from 6366 g (steel) to 5968 g (aluminium). The README partly explains this ('because it counts bar stock as makeable') but never states the total. 3.
evidence.fitness: A researcher could extend it (sized rods plug into the closure model), but the result is not new: the fourth-root modulus scaling d_Al/d_steel=(E_s/E_Al)^(1/4) is textbook beam theory, and aluminium guide shafts with polymer bushings are established commercial practice (igus drylin hard-anodised aluminium shafts; OpenBuilds V-slot aluminium extrusion with wheels in many RepRap-derived machines), none cited. Nearest prior in-repo work is selfrep-rodbeam, which already sized wood; this adds one material row. Missing: a baseline comparing to aluminium extrusion/V-slot frames, any wear or surface-hardness analysis, bearing redesign for a non-8 mm rod, and the penalty-budget search the README defers. 2.
evidence.domain: Against machine-element practice (Shigley's Mechanical Engineering Design, shafts; igus drylin shaft guidance): the beam sizing is correct, but (1) a guide rod under a carriage is better modelled with the load at the worst position plus self-weight, and two rods sharing the load; (2) untreated 6061 (about 95 HB) galls in bushings, which is why vendors hard-anodise, and the README only says 'optimistic'; (3) a 10.4 mm rod does not fit LM8UU or 8 mm printed bushings and clamps at all, so the 12 mm 'holder limit' hides a redesign of every bushing and rod clamp whose masses the model leaves unchanged; (4) hardwood E=10 GPa is at the low end of handbook values. 2.

verdict: A small, honest computed note: every number in the README reproduces on rerun and against my own Euler-Bernoulli recomputation from Gere & Goodno with handbook moduli (steel sag 0.192 mm, aluminium 10.44 mm, hardwood 16.9 mm, rod masses, closures 39.5/37.8/28.7%), and its assumptions are labelled. It misses the bar on verification: all five mutations I seeded in alu.py survived the six tests, which mainly re-test the sibling beam model. Fitness and domain are 2: the stiffness result is textbook, aluminium guide shafts are established commercial practice not cited, and the 12 mm holder assumption hides that a 10.4 mm rod needs new bushings and clamps.
